name: CapCut Switch Focus Depth Blur
use_when: A documentary, explainer, historical comparison, or character contrast scene needs to move attention from one cutout subject to another.
Two images or source elements can be separated into foreground layers over a background.
The editor wants a rack-focus style handoff using scale, position, blur, and subtle background motion inside CapCut.
avoid_when: Both subjects need to be read at the same time.
The cutout edges are too rough to survive blur, scale, or phone-size review.
The scene is evidence-critical and artificial depth would make source material feel less trustworthy.

timeline_pattern.pattern: background -> cutout_left -> cutout_right -> remove_background -> feather_masks -> enhance_if_needed -> compound_cutouts -> scale_position_keyframes -> cross_blur_layers -> background_countermove -> optional_fps_lag_pendulum -> qc
timeline_pattern.layer_rule: Use at least three elements: background, first cutout subject, and second cutout subject.
timeline_pattern.compound_rule: Compound only the foreground image layers before the main move so their shared pan/scale can be controlled cleanly.
timeline_pattern.focus_rule: One subject should sharpen as the other softens; avoid a middle section where both are unreadable.
timeline_pattern.background_rule: Move the background more subtly than the foreground so the scene gains depth instead of sliding as one flat image.

motion.rule: Use eased scale and X/Y motion to hand off attention, then use opposite blur ramps to simulate focus depth.

keyframe_values.foreground_move_window: A usable starting range is roughly 1s to 3s for the main focus handoff.
keyframe_values.scale_start_end: Foreground compound can start around 125% scale and end around 135% when the crop remains safe.
keyframe_values.blur_handoff: Outgoing subject can ramp blur from 0 to 50 while incoming subject ramps from 50 to 0.
keyframe_values.background_scale: Background can move more gently, such as about 120% to 125%, with smaller position drift than the foreground.
keyframe_values.easing: Apply Ease or Cubic Ease to scale, X, and Y curves after keyframes are placed.
keyframe_values.texture_optional: For subtle documentary texture, FPS Lag around 14 and Play Pendulum around speed 2, strength 3, twist 0, sharpen 0 can be tested after readability passes.

sound.rule: Usually no hit is needed; use a soft riser or low whoosh only if the focus handoff is a real story beat and speech stays clear.

captions.rule: Keep captions away from the subject receiving focus and suppress them during the blur handoff if they compete with the comparison.

color.rule: Match cutouts to the background before adding texture; blur and scale should not hide edge mismatch or source quality problems.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use alpha cutouts, scale/crop/overlay keyframes, boxblur or gblur ramps per subject, and a separate slower background transform; render focus-handoff contact sheets.
implementation.remotion: Create a SwitchFocusDepthBlur component with foreground assets, background asset, focusStartFrame, focusEndFrame, scale/position values, blur ramps, and caption-safe regions.
implementation.blender: Use image planes or cards at different depths with camera or object motion and depth-of-field blur, then render with safe framing.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Place background plus two images, use Remove Background and feathered rectangle masks, enhance low-quality cutouts if needed, compound the cutouts, keyframe scale/position from the first subject to the second, apply eased graphs, then use duplicated blur effect layers inside each subject compound with opposite 0/50 blur ramps.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use nested foreground cutouts, Motion keyframes with Ease In/Out, Gaussian Blur keyframes per nested subject, and a subtler background scale/position move.

common_mistakes: Compounding the background with the cutouts so no parallax depth remains.
Leaving harsh rectangular mask edges around cutouts.
Using blur so heavily that neither subject is readable during the transition.
Moving foreground and background by the same amount, which makes the scene feel flat.
Adding FPS lag or pendulum before the focus handoff is readable.
qc: Does the viewer know which subject is primary before, during, and after the focus switch?
Do cutout edges remain clean after Remove Background, feathering, scale, and blur?
Is at least one subject readable throughout the handoff?
Does background motion stay subtler than foreground motion?
Do captions and source labels avoid the focused subject and remain readable at delivery size?
